3. RFC alignment of this change

The reviewed change preserves the relevant Kerberos boundaries. RFC 4120 §3.2.4 permits a server-selected subkey in AP-REP and protects the reply with the ticket session key. §3.2.5 requires client decryption and matching authenticator timestamps before retaining the returned subkey. The candidate keeps those modeled stages and adds only the missing host-local provenance.

RFC 4121 §2 defines the acceptor-subkey preference for subsequent per-message protection when that key is asserted. The selected Windows AES profile already models this distinction; WIN-11 neither changes the early initiator key nor substitutes the acceptor key for AP-REP protection. The RFC permits an acceptor subkey; this report does not claim that every Kerberos exchange must generate one.

MS-KILE §3.1.1.2 supplies the selected Windows AES distinction between AP-REQ and AP-REP subkeys. MS-CSSP §3.1.5 supplies the last-client-token/public-key-binding ordering. The preserved early-binding model is consistent with that timing; the local-origin operation does not move the exchange or credential-disclosure boundary.

Primary RFC text was consulted for this review. The result is a scoped conformance check of the changed educational model and preserved transitions. It is not fresh certification of every existing protocol, a numerical cryptography audit or a live Windows/CredSSP interoperability result.

4. Usability and native-evidence assessment

Starting replay at H’s creation fixes the concrete learning problem: the key no longer first appears when C verifies it. Local operation, creator, current holder and later client acquisition remain distinguishable. The inspected final RCG origin capture visibly shows the H-local creation and CREATE field-history step.

The fresh mounted checks verify the interval boundary explicitly: no holder before creation begins, H alone after creation completes, then one plaintext holding per peer after C’s validation. The three-moment key path ends at accepted mechanism context; completing it does not by itself exercise a later binding or logon denial. An initial reviewer probe selected Resume for a single-step queue instead of the inspector’s complete-path replay control. That setup failure is retained and explained; the corrected checks pass without a product change.

The worker reports eighteen browser cases: six fixed presets in source HTTP, standalone HTTP and standalone file:, using Chromium 155.0.8059.84. The record identifies actual picker, field-index and seek-control interactions, captures and candidate hash. These records were checked, and supplied images were visually inspected; no independent native browser run was performed here. No browser executable was available in this reviewer environment.

The accepted image uses a taller 1480 × 1600 capture viewport to show the map without the sticky-toolbar overlap seen in a retained rejected attempt; the recorded interaction cases use 1480 × 1000. That capture is useful origin evidence, not proof of every viewport or general accessibility. The absent retained native runner/session command record is a reproducibility limitation, not proof that the reported session did not occur. G01 speech/comprehension, actual touch/zoom, cross-engine checks and performance remain outside this narrow acceptance.

5. Detailed comments for the worker

W11-F1 · Preserve a bounded creator-origin follow-up

The disclosed sibling omissions are real, unchanged teaching gaps. Keep them tracked separately from the accepted acceptor-subkey repair. Current representative examples include KDC-created TGT/service-ticket keys whose field history starts at the recipient’s store, downstream equivalents, an inner TLS key starting at verification, and an outer TLS key with no field-only moment. The current evidence is a representative inspection, not an exhaustive audit.

Before claiming general origin completeness, inventory keys with canonical creation but missing creator-local field operations. Derive any operation from the artifact’s actual creator, not the carrier sender: the grouped TLS response is H-to-C while these modeled TLS key artifacts declare C as creator. Preserve canonical effects, receipt/verification boundaries and current wire membership. Never “fix” discoverability by sending plaintext secret keys. Include an existing correct local-create path and a key whose creator differs from the carrier sender as controls. Keep this work bounded and do not silently fold it into WIN-11’s completed claim.

W11-F2 · Make the next package portable

review-package-status.json and SHA256SUMS.txt are valid supplied attachments, but neither is inside the verification archive. This is nonblocking for this review because the full supplied set is available. It falls short of the next plan’s portable-handoff requirement. The copied handoff also keeps repository-relative links, so it is not independently navigable from an arbitrary downloads folder.

At the next packaging step, include an internal package manifest/checksum list covering the source archive, standalone and evidence members, and retain an external final-artifact checksum list for the completed verification ZIP. Avoid a self-referential requirement for a ZIP to contain its own final hash. Clearly label internal versus outer-package checksums. Preserve old packages, make extraction instructions explicit, and ensure handoff links resolve within the delivered layout. This metadata correction does not require another product test sweep.

W11-F3 · Retain reproducible native evidence

For the next actual native validation, retain the runnable check or exact session-command/action record with hashes, runtime/browser version, viewport and source/standalone identities. Keep interactive browser observations separate from mounted DOM tests and from source-model comparisons. The current manual instructions help reproduction, but cannot reproduce the eighteen captured session snapshots as a program. Do not retroactively invent a runner for a past session or claim this reviewer reran it.

W11-F4 · Gate deployment before the next publication

The supplied .github/workflows/pages.yml starts on main pushes and its deploy job depends only on its own build job. The separate CI workflow runs vectors/tests, but Pages does not depend on its success. This confirms the disclosed pipeline gap from the archived workflow configuration; external run history was not checked.

Fix this separately before a future publication: deployment must consume a successful CI result for the same trusted main commit/artifact. A failed CI result must prevent deploy, and a manual path must preserve the intended gate. Do not treat this WIN-11 acceptance as authorization to publish or as evidence that the pipeline has been corrected.

6. Next step and worker handoff

Send this HTML review to the worker. It is the complete review handoff; there is no second reviewer-notes file to merge. Keep auth-flow-studio-next-expansion-worker-plan.html as the implementation plan.

  1. Update the candidate disposition to record scoped independent WIN-11 acceptance and retain the exact reviewed hashes. Keep the sibling-origin follow-up and the packaging/native-evidence comments visible.
  2. Continue P0-B: accepted-build performance characterization and measured optimization. Preserve the exact previous accepted HTML and this candidate as separately identified inputs; neither this review nor a new baseline clears older performance flags.
  3. Continue P0-C navigation and accessibility preparation, then P1 NFS according to the existing phase order. G01 remains open until the required human assistive-technology observation is recorded.
  4. Keep the remainder of the plan unchanged: 81 core scenarios, four optional extensions, and the existing accepted catalog preserved. This delivery adds none of those new scenarios and does not complete P0 as a whole.

Stop additional testing of unchanged WIN-11 code once these bounded results are recorded. Broaden testing when a later shared authoring, state, renderer or navigation change creates a concrete new regression risk.
